Tell me, whilst you were in the police station, did you see Mr. Zaric?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You know Mr. Zaric, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. And very well, because we were born in the same place and we practically grew up there as I've already stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now tell me, how often did you have the opportunity to see Mr. Zaric in the police station in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: Well, I can say that I saw Simo Zaric several times. Could have been five or six times in the police station. I -- at that time, I was also in the police station, and all that went on I could discuss it with him. And he also claimed that all -- that something should be done about things that were going on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let us try to speed matters up, that is, I will ask you questions, and just answer that. That is only what I ask you and to try to go through this in this particular order. So will you tell me, you told me that you saw him several times, it could have been five or six. Now, tell me this: What uniform did Simo Zaric wear on those five or six occasions when you saw him in the police station?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: Simo had a military uniform, an olive-green-grey uniform. Later on, I used to see him in a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Tell me only if you can answer with yes or no, on those five or six occasions when you saw Simo Zaric, did you -- were you also able to talk with him? Just tell me yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, during those conversations with Mr. Zaric, did you learn how did it come about that he came to the police station, that he was in the police station?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Explain to the Court what is it that Mr. Zaric told you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: On that occasion, Zaric told me that he was in the police station in order to collect information necessary and important for military security and that that was due to the orders of Commander Stevan Nikolic and Radovan Antic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Simo Zaric told you that on one of those occasions when you talked with him, is it?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, who did Mr. Zaric usually go to see when he came to the police station?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: He went to see the inspectors in the Criminal Investigation Department, Sarkanovic and the technician Zoran Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is sorry. The interpreter missed the first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When you say "the Criminal Investigation Department" --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...in the transcript

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the interpreter said they didn't catch one of the names, the first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So, sir, in the transcript it says that he went to see Sarkanovic. Will you give us Sarkanovic's first name, and the other two persons that you mentioned in addition to Sarkanovic as members of the Criminal Investigation Department?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: Vladimir Sarkanovic, Milos Savic, Zoran Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you know if Mr. Zaric when in the police station had interviews or an interview, whichever, with one of the detained individuals?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: Well, I remember how he -- that he interviewed Sulejman Tihic, the then SDA president in Bosanski Samac, and some other individuals whom I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Tell me, did -- during that time, during the time that you were there, was Simo Zaric, to the best of your knowledge, ever a member of the police? Was he, Mr. Zaric?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: No, never. He was never a member of the police during the war. And if you mean the time of the war, he was never a member or part of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That is what we are interested in, that is, the time of war. Otherwise, we know that Mr. Zaric used to work for the police during some years before the war, but that is not of relevance here. So we are asking only about that time whilst you were in the station and during the war, that is, your testimony is that he was never a member of the police. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you see Simo Zaric beat, harass, insult any of the detainees when you were there?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: No. Simo Zaric is not such a person, nor was it his style. Simo Zaric always conducted himself in accordance with social norms and things that happened in the police station were just as odious to him as they were to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could Simo Zaric issue orders to the police?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: No, Zaric couldn't do that. Stevan Todorovic was the only one who could do that, as the chief of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now that you mention Stevan Todorovic, can you describe -- explain to us in your own words, what were the relations between Stevan Todorovic and Simo Zaric? From what you could see, from what you could conclude or perhaps what you heard from somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: Well, you see, the two of them were on bad terms. To begin with, because Simo as an individual and as a man always tried to do something just, to do something proper. And in public, he always pointed out at the bad traits of Stevan Todorovic, or perhaps there was something, I don't know. Perhaps they had fallen out over some personal matter, but I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was Stevan Todorovic as chief of police superior to Zaric in any way?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: No, because Zaric was under the army command, and therefore part of the JNA. So that Simo Zaric had no jurisdiction, had no competence, to undertake anything in the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. But what I wanted was -- my question had to do whether Stevan Todorovic could issue any orders to Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: No, he couldn't. And that was I think one of the reasons for the bad terms on which the two of them were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you only one question more, sir, before we adjourn for the day. In the police station, and we've already heard a certain number of people and not such a small one, with regard to the way in which the police station operated, but tell me who is it that decided who should be arrested and kept under custody in the police station?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: In relation to decisions concerning the arrest and detention of individuals in the Detention Unit, that is, the police station, Stevan Todorovic was the only one who was authorised to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC
utterances.text: May I only add something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. Do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] None of the other employees in the security service had authority to do that. The chief of the police station, and that is Stevan Todorovic, was the only one who had such powers, that is, neither the commander nor the criminal investigation inspectors nor any one of the policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. We will rise now and continue our proceedings tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: at 1.46 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 8th day of April, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 25
